item.title: Slides: several periods of one target across long gaps
item.description: The illustrated companion to the spec 033 write-up: joining by gap
item.content:encoded:
The illustrated companion to the spec 033 write-up: joining by gap length, what holding course does to every system, and how well the gap history is chosen beyond about an hour.

What the figures show​

  • Bands: ctl alone ÷ the joint solve by the gap before a later period, in both runs, with 95% engagement intervals.
  • Systems: median range error of ctl alone, the joint solve and k4 on later periods, in both runs.
  • Evidence: for each engagement with a gap of at least 70 min (ownship holding course), the log evidence of the true gap history minus the declared one, against alone ÷ joint.

Reproducing the figures​

uv run python scripts/research/tl12_charts.py --out-dir site/static/img/2026-11-21-long-gaps-slides

The script reads only the committed records (results branches results/timelate-tl-q-dev-44691013700, results/timelate-tl-q-hold-dev-44741196091 and results/tl12ev-tl12ev-hold-44803371523); each figure's .json sidecar names the inputs' digests and the commit.

item.title: Several periods of one target across long gaps: what joining depends on
item.description: Spec 025 found that one solve through the gaps beats solving each period of a target alone,
item.content:encoded:
Spec 025 found that one solve through the gaps beats solving each period of a target alone, across gaps of 5 to 30 minutes. This development study stretched the gaps to 30–90 minutes. It ran twice on one spent seed: once with an ownship that turns often, and once with one that holds course. Nothing was trained and nothing here is a registered result.

What the data support, as narrowed by the review panel:

  • Joining helps a period that has no ownship turn of its own, by about 2, across gaps under about 70 minutes.
  • Beyond 70 minutes the readings fall below 1 in both runs, but they are not separated.
  • The true gap structure would still help there. What falls short is choosing the gap history: in most engagements the evidence does not prefer the true one.

The illustrated companion is the slides post.

What was run​

  • Engagements: 40 six-hour engagements from the long simulator (specs 023–026), with Annex B targets and no realism layer.
  • Layout: each engagement is cut into 2 to 4 periods of 15–30 minutes, with gaps of 30–90 minutes.
  • Two runs on the same engagements, targets and layouts:
    • the ownship turns every 20–40 minutes;
    • the ownship holds each leg 1–2 hours.
  • Systems, unchanged from spec 030:
    • ctl alone on each period;
    • the joint solve over the span, with the gaps' bearings masked;
    • the carried prior k4.
  • Seed: spent seed 348.
  • Diagnostic: on the 21 engagements with a gap of at least 70 minutes, the evidence of the declared gap history was compared with the true history fitted the same way.

What it found​

turning every 20–40 minholding 1–2 h
later periods with their own turn0.780.23
median error: alone / joint / k40.117 / 0.121 / 0.1120.273 / 0.174 / 0.188
alone ÷ joint, all periods1.20 [0.90, 1.60] (109)1.34 [1.010, 1.84] (92)
… gap 30–50 / 50–70 / 70–90 min1.40 / 1.27 / 0.801.34 / 2.85 [1.49, 6.05] / 0.71 [0.47, 1.02]
… periods without their own turn, gaps under 70 min2.24 [1.13, 4.50]2.13 [1.29, 3.55]
alone ÷ k40.941.05
  • Whether a period has its own ownship turn matters most. Without one, joining helps by about 2, separated in both runs below 70 minutes. With one, it reads 1.1–1.25, not separated. On rows a period determines alone, alone ÷ joint is 0.89 in both runs.
  • Gap length.
    • Of 18 band intervals one is separated: holding course, 50–70 minutes.
    • A trend with gap length is not separated in either run.
    • In the turning run the median period at 50–70 minutes favours ctl alone (0.80).
    • The bands were chosen after looking at the data.
  • Beyond 70 minutes the geometric means read below 1 in both runs (0.80, 0.71), with medians 0.95 and 0.88. Neither is separated. The two runs barely agree period by period (r = 0.15), so they are not a replication.
  • Holding course roughly doubles everyone's error (by geometric mean; the median for alone rises by 1.49).
  • k4, as tuned on spec 030's short gaps and propagated at constant velocity, is level with ctl alone. After an hour its uncertainty covers almost everything.
  • Cost. The joint solve takes 11 to 16 times as long as ctl alone.

Beyond about an hour: the gap history is not chosen well​

  • The information exists given the history. The span fitted with the true gap structure still beats ctl alone beyond 70 minutes: 2.35 [0.96, 5.98] holding course, 2.48 [1.30, 4.90] turning. The joint solve is about 3 times that reference's error.
  • The evidence rarely separates the true gap history from a simpler one. The joint solve declares fewer manoeuvres than happened: 123 against 178.
    • In most engagements the Laplace evidence does not prefer the true history.
    • Most differences are within ±10 units: the declared history is better by more than 10 in 5 engagements, the truth in 3.
    • Search shortfall is a minority.
  • Whether a better search would help is not resolved. The diagnostic's re-run ran on another CPU family. In 5 of 21 engagements it declared a different history from the scored run, so its cross-tabulation against errors is not a result.
  • A limit of the comparison. The "true" history is a prior-fitted Laplace mode, and pairing defects of 1–3.5 nats are known.

What it supports, and what not​

  • A suggestion, not a rule: join a period that has no ownship turn of its own with its neighbours across gaps up to about an hour. Beyond that, nothing here shows that joining helps or harms. This is one spent seed, with bands chosen after the data.
  • Not to be claimed:
    • that joining fails beyond an hour;
    • that the limit is identifiability rather than search;
    • that carried priors carry nothing in general.
  • Limits:
    • the long simulator's ownship steers on the true target;
    • C″'s start reads only the first ownship turn;
    • 20 to 30 periods per band.

The time-late gap track​

specresult
025joining beats solving alone across gaps of 5–30 min (registered)
027a carried start does not substitute for joining (registered)
030a carried prior helps a period that cannot answer alone, but does not replace joining (registered)
033across 30–90 min gaps joining still helps periods without their own turn below about an hour; beyond, nothing is shown (development)

A per-period consistency flag was judged not worth registering (experiments/20261120-tl11-flag-look/).

What follows is the owner's choice:

  1. Stop here.
  2. Register a gap × own-turn rule on fresh seeds (369 onward), with enough periods per band.
  3. First, a development check of the evidence on the scored run's own histories.

Records:

  • experiments/20261120-tl12-dev/;
  • experiments/20261120-tl12-hold-dev/, with evidence/ and the panel's review.md;
  • spec specs/033-long-gaps/.

This study was developed as spec 031 and renumbered after another session's 031 and 032 merged first.

item.title: Slides: the carried prior where the ownship's legs outlast the window
item.description: These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up. On
item.content:encoded:
These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up. On blind 2-hour windows, ctl ÷ ctl-prior is 1.54 [1.16, 2.03] ("ctl-prior better"). Against a joint solve over the same past bearings it is 1.11 (not separated). There is no harm. Spec: specs/032-long-legs/.

What was built​

  • The scorer: src/tma2/long/study32.py, run by tma2-long study32.
  • jointheld always writes its .npz.
  • Configs: configs/long/legs-{tuning,val,test}.json and run files configs/long/runs/legs-*.json.
  • Scripts: scripts/research/legs_{digests,charts}.py.
  • Tests: tests/unit/test_long_study32.py.
  • Records:
    • tuning: experiments/20261120-legs-tuning/;
    • decision: 20261120-legs-decision/;
    • validation: 20261120-legs-val/;
    • test: 20261120-legs/, with review.md.

What was not achieved​

  • Unscored: the windows where contact was lost (half the blind windows).
  • Untested: ordinary ranges with the ownship holding course, and chains of blind windows.
  • Not calibrated: the carried uncertainty, which is not a stated uncertainty.

What comes next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended: adopt 2-hour ctl-prior for the tended contact, and close the track with a synthesis.
  • Alternatives:
    • an E2 study at ordinary ranges;
    • repair the hand-over;
    • lost-contact prediction.

Figures: scripts/research/legs_charts.py, with a sidecar beside each SVG.

item.title: Long engagements: the carried prior where the ownship's legs outlast the window
item.description: The owner's hypothesis: knowledge of the previous track can usefully constrain the solution for
item.content:encoded:
The owner's hypothesis: knowledge of the previous track can usefully constrain the solution for the next leg. Spec 031 found that with ownship legs of 1–2 h, the standing 2-hour window always contains a turn, so the prior had nothing to rescue. This study makes the ownship hold each leg for 2–4 h, so some standing 2-hour windows are blind.

The result: on blind 2-hour windows, ctl ÷ ctl-prior is 1.54 [1.16, 2.03], and the registered rule reads "ctl-prior better". Against a joint solve over the same past bearings it is 1.11 [0.84, 1.45], not separated. The prior does no harm on windows with one turn; it helps there too, at 1.26.

Spec: specs/032-long-legs/. Record: experiments/20261120-legs/.

The design​

  • Engagements: spec 024's realism, with ownship legs of 2–4 h, contact 1, and 6- and 12-hour engagements.
  • Windows: the standing configuration, 2-hour windows overlapping 30 min.
  • Systems on blind (turn-free) windows:
    • ctl, the window solved alone;
    • ctl-prior, which carries the previous window's state and covariance as a prior, with spec 028's guard;
    • a joint solve: ctl on the window and the one before it, 3.5 h of past bearings.
  • Estimands:
    • E1 = ctl ÷ ctl-prior; E2 = joint ÷ ctl-prior.
    • Harm is read on one-turn windows.
    • Each is a geometric mean of per-window median range error, with a bootstrap over engagements.
  • Registration: before seeds 367 and 368 existed. The test was raised to 50 + 50 engagements on tuning's yield (experiments/20261120-legs-decision/).

What happened​

Test: seed 368, 100 engagements, scored once. Soundness passed.

readingrangemedianctl-prior bettertwice as good / twice as bad
E1 ctl ÷ ctl-prior1.537 [1.156, 2.029]1.2559%38% / 18%
E2 joint ÷ ctl-prior1.113 [0.840, 1.445]1.2461%24% / 19%
harm (one-turn windows)1.259 [1.056, 1.500]1.2160%31% / 16%

  • Median range error on decided blind windows:

    systemmedian error
    ctl16.7%
    joint12.8%
    ctl-prior10.4%
    reference told the true history3.3%

  • The prior does the work, not the carried start: ctl-carry ÷ ctl-prior is 1.52.

  • The forecasts came true: E1 "better" (probability 0.45), E2 "not separated" (0.5), no harm (0.95).

What the panel narrowed​

Three reviewers each approved with findings (experiments/20261120-legs/review.md). Every decided number was reproduced independently.

  • Half the blind windows are outside the claim.
    • Holding a 2–4 h leg opens the range, often beyond detection. 80 of 165 blind windows were lost to contact (median 72 km) and are unscored.
    • The claim covers the 85 where contact held: median 37 km, about half the bearings detected.
  • It is a far-range effect.
    • E1 is about 2.2 beyond 35 km and about 1.0 under; at 15–25 km it is 0.82.
    • Range and contact loss move together here and cannot be separated.
  • E1 is "more data beats no data". E2 is the fair comparison, and the compact hand-over is not shown to lose to keeping the bearings, nor to beat them.
  • The prior comes from a window that saw a turn in 83 of 85 cases. Chains of blind windows are untested.
  • Seeds move.
    • E1 was 1.32, 0.87 and 1.54 across the three seeds; pooled, it is 1.37 [1.05, 1.80].
    • The joint solve against ctl flipped between seeds; pooled, it is not separated.
  • The carried uncertainty is not calibrated. It is too wide in the core and too narrow in the tail, and covers 0.79 across a turn.
  • Limits:
    • windows are placed past true manoeuvres;
    • spec 028's hand-over defect is kept;
    • one simulator, contact 1.

What it means for the owner's question​

A qualified yes.

  • Where the ownship holds course through the whole window and the target is far, the previous track constrains the next window far better than the window alone: about twice as well beyond 35 km.
  • It does about as well as re-solving the previous bearings, and needs only four numbers and a covariance.

At ordinary ranges the benefit is not shown. Where contact is lost, nothing in this design answers well.

Next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended default:
    • Adopt 2-hour ctl-prior with its guard as the standing chained system for the tended contact, up to 12 h, within the limits above.
    • Keep the joint solve as the equal alternative where the bearings are kept.
    • Close the long-engagement track with one synthesis of specs 023 to 032.
  • Alternatives:
    • an E2 study at ordinary ranges (15–25 km, range kept while holding course);
    • repair the hand-over and the process-noise shape, then check coverage across a turn;
    • predict through lost-contact windows and score both systems there.

Slides: the slides post.

item.title: Kickoff: the carried prior where the ownship's legs outlast the 2-hour window
item.description: Spec 031 found that a 1-hour window with a carried prior is
item.content:encoded:
Spec 031 found that a 1-hour window with a carried prior is no substitute for a longer window or a joint solve. But with ownship legs of 1–2 h, a 2-hour window always contains a turn. The owner's case is a leg longer than the standing 2-hour window, so that the window itself is blind. Spec: specs/032-long-legs/.

Where we are​

  • Standing: ctl on 2-hour windows, with spec 028's ctl-prior (the previous window's state and uncertainty as a prior, with a guard) for tended contacts.
  • Spec 029: on blind 1-hour windows the prior beat the window alone (about 1.7 to 2.4).
  • Spec 031:
    • A joint solve over the same past bearings beat the 1-hour prior (0.774 [0.632, 0.954]).
    • Not tested: legs longer than the 2-hour window.

Where this task moves to​

  • Engagements: the ownship holds each leg for 2–4 h, with the same realism. The range drifts out, so about half of bearings are lost at long range.
  • Systems on turn-free 2-hour windows:
    • 2-hour ctl;
    • 2-hour ctl-prior;
    • a joint solve: ctl on the window and the one before it, 3.5 h, past bearings only.
  • Rules:
    • E1 = ctl ÷ ctl-prior; E2 = joint ÷ ctl-prior. Each ends "ctl-prior better", "worse" or "not separated".
    • Harm: E1 on one-turn windows has its upper limit below 1.
  • Plan:
    1. tuning on spent seed 366;
    2. the decision record;
    3. validation on seed 367;
    4. test on seed 368, scored once;
    5. the panel, then the write-up.
  • Risks:
    • Lost contact thins the turn-free windows. Held windows are far-range windows.
    • The joint solve's cost on 3.5 h is unknown.

How progress will be shown​

  • E1 and E2 with intervals, and per-window ratios.
  • Errors by system, by range band and by detected share.
  • Guard rate, and coverage and NEES of the 2-hour hand-overs.
  • Compute per engagement-hour.

item.title: Slides: the carried prior against longer windows
item.description: These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up.
item.content:encoded:
These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up. On turn-free 1-hour windows, a joint solve over the hour and the hour before it beats 1-hour ctl-prior: 0.774 [0.632, 0.954]. The 2-hour systems also beat it. The registered rule reads "ctl-prior worse" three times. Spec: specs/031-held-comparators/.

What was built​

  • The jointheld part of tma2-long: ctl on each turn-free window's union with its predecessor.
  • The scorer: src/tma2/long/study30.py, run by tma2-long study30.
  • CI: long.yml passes a tag and the window settings through.
  • Configs: configs/long/cmp-{val,test}.json and run files configs/long/runs/cmp-*.json.
  • Scripts: scripts/research/cmp_{digests,supplement,charts}.py.
  • Records:
    • tuning: experiments/20261119-cmp-tuning/;
    • decision: 20261120-cmp-decision/;
    • validation: 20261120-cmp-val/;
    • test: 20261120-cmp/, with review.md and supplement.json.

What was not achieved​

  • Untested: legs longer than the 2-hour window, which is the owner's blind case at the standing configuration.
  • Not measured separately: each system's own cost, and the 2-hour hand-overs' guard rate and coverage.
  • Not decided: whether 2-hour ctl-prior beats 2-hour ctl. Here it is supplement only.

What comes next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended: close the long-engagement track with a synthesis.
  • Alternatives:
    • legs longer than the window;
    • reopen with new information.

Figures: scripts/research/cmp_charts.py, with a sidecar beside each SVG.

item.title: Long engagements: the carried prior against longer windows
item.description: Spec 029 found that on held-course 1-hour windows, carrying the previous window's state as a
item.content:encoded:
Spec 029 found that on held-course 1-hour windows, carrying the previous window's state as a prior (ctl-prior) beats solving the window alone. Its panel called that "more data beats no data" and asked for the fair comparisons: ctl on its standing 2-hour windows, and a joint solve over the turn-free hour and the hour before it.

The result: the registered rule reads "ctl-prior worse" against every comparator. The clean comparison is the joint solve. It uses the same past as the carried prior and no later bearings, and its error is 0.774 [0.632, 0.954] of the prior's. A 1-hour window with a carried prior is not a substitute for using the bearings themselves.

Spec: specs/031-held-comparators/. Record: experiments/20261120-cmp/.

The design​

  • Engagements: spec 029's held-course engagements: ownship legs of 1–2 h, the tended contact, 60 engagements of 6 and 12 h.
  • Systems, each on its own windows and read on the same turn-free 1-hour windows:
    • (a) 1-hour ctl-prior, spec 029's system;
    • (b) ctl and ctl-prior on 2-hour windows overlapping 30 min, stitched mid-overlap;
    • (c) ctl on the union of the turn-free hour and the hour before it: the joint solve.
  • Estimands, each comparator's error ÷ (a)'s in range, as a geometric mean with a bootstrap over engagements:
    • D1: 2-hour ctl;
    • D2: the joint solve;
    • D3: 2-hour ctl-prior, added on tuning before validation.
  • Rule: "ctl-prior better" or "worse" when the interval excludes 1. The rule was registered before seeds 365 and 366 existed (experiments/20261120-cmp-decision/).

What happened​

Test: seed 366. 179 decided turn-free windows from 56 engagements, scored once. Soundness passed.

comparator ÷ 1-hour ctl-priorrangemedian(a) better(a) twice as bad
D1: 2-hour ctl0.730 [0.579, 0.917]0.9043%35%
D2: joint solve0.774 [0.632, 0.954]0.7841%37%
D3: 2-hour ctl-prior0.488 [0.386, 0.619]0.5826%45%

  • Course and speed agree in direction, with intervals wholly below 1.

  • Median range error on turn-free windows:

    systemmedian error
    1-hour ctl22.4%
    1-hour ctl-prior10.2%
    2-hour ctl9.0%
    joint solve7.0%
    2-hour ctl-prior4.2%

  • Spec 029's gain replicates at 1.71 [1.40, 2.14]. Quote it as about 1.7 to 2.4.

  • The forecasts were 1.1–1.3 for D1 and D2, and wrong in direction. Tuning had pointed that way on about 34 windows, but it compared (a) from spec 029's run on another CPU family with (b) and (c) from this run, which spec 024's gotcha forbids. D3's forecast was right in direction, and the effect was larger than forecast.

What the panel narrowed​

Three reviewers each approved with findings (experiments/20261120-cmp/review.md). Every decided number was reproduced independently.

  • D2 is the clean comparison.

    • D1 and D3 take 98% of their rows from a 2-hour window that contains an ownship turn, and that window runs a median of 29 min past the hour.
    • So they also measure geometry and latency. The joint solve has neither advantage and still wins.

  • These are averages with wide spread. The 1-hour prior is better in about 4 windows in 10 and twice as bad in about a third.

  • The readings are conservative. Four windows where 1-hour ctl-prior gave no answer at all are excluded, and the comparators answered all four.

  • Heterogeneity. D2 is 0.62 on 6-hour engagements and 0.90 [0.69, 1.17] on 12-hour ones.

  • 2-hour ctl-prior is not shown best here.

    • Its edge over 2-hour ctl (1.49 held, median 1.14; 1.26 one-turn, median 1.01) is supplement only, and validation went the other way.
    • The registered support for it is spec 028's test.

  • Cost and latency. Per engagement-hour, the 2-hour job costs about 2.1× the 1-hour one, but both run several systems, so no single system's cost is known. A 2-hour estimate waits for up to an hour of later bearings and updates every 90 min instead of 45.

  • Limits:

    • ownship legs of 1–2 h;
    • contact 1;
    • one simulator;
    • windows placed past true target manoeuvres;
    • spec 028's hand-over defect kept.

    Legs longer than the standing 2-hour window, the owner's blind case at the standing configuration, were not tested.

What it means for the owner's question​

The previous track does constrain a blind leg: spec 029 shows that. But the same past bearings used directly in a joint fit constrain it better than a Gaussian summary of them. The carried prior compresses the past into four numbers and a covariance. Where those bearings are available, fitting them beats summarising them.

Spec 029's recommendation, ctl-prior on 1-hour windows, is withdrawn. What stands is spec 028's: ctl-prior with its guard on 2-hour windows for tended contacts up to 12 h.

Next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended default: close the long-engagement track as a simulation study, with ctl on 2-hour windows and spec 028's ctl-prior standing. Write one synthesis of specs 023 to 030.
  • Alternatives:
    • Legs longer than the window: ownship legs of 2–4 h with 2-hour windows, compared on past bearings only, reporting the 2-hour hand-overs' guard rate and coverage.
    • Reopen with new information: measured realism, an ownship steered by its own track, or association.

Slides: the slides post.

item.content:encoded:
The illustrated companion to the spec 030 write-up: the registered comparison, where the carried prior helps, and how well its stated uncertainty covers the truth.

What the figures show​

  • Verdict: alone ÷ k4 and k4 ÷ joint in range on every split, periods after an engagement's first, with 95% engagement intervals.
  • Kinds: alone ÷ the carried prior, uninflated and k4, for periods with and without an ownship turn of their own (Annex B and busier).
  • Coverage: the truth's squared distance from the carried prior at a period's first row, as a cumulative distribution against a calibrated one (Annex B).

Reproducing the figures​

The script reads only the committed record (results branch results/timelate-tl-o-test-44618826527, seed 363); each figure's .json sidecar names the inputs' digests and the commit.

item.title: A carried prior across gaps: it helps where a period cannot answer alone
item.description: Spec 027 showed that carrying a start from one period to the next does not substitute for one
item.content:encoded:
Spec 027 showed that carrying a start from one period to the next does not substitute for one solve through the gaps. This registered study carried information instead. The previous period's declared state and its uncertainty become a prior on the next period's starting state. By the rule registered beforehand, the carried prior helps against solving each period alone on Annex B targets, and no harm was shown. The review panel approved and narrowed the result:

  • the gain is in periods the bearings leave undetermined;
  • the 4× inflation chosen in development is not shown to matter;
  • the carried uncertainty covers the truth because it is too wide.

The joint solve stays the standing system. Nothing was trained. The illustrated companion is the slides post.

What was built​

For each period after an engagement's first, the evidence of the standing control ctl gains a Gaussian prior on the period's starting state (position, course, speed). That prior is built in three steps:

  1. Take the previous period's declared track at its last row.
  2. Take that state's Laplace covariance from the previous period's posterior fit.
  3. Run both through the gap at constant velocity. Annex B's manoeuvre rate and sizes are added as process noise.

The prior replaces the standing prior's terms for those four parameters (range log-uniform, bearing and course uniform, a soft speed band), and the period's search starts from the carried state. Everything else in ctl is unchanged.

How k4 was chosen​

Development used spent seeds only.

  • Seed 361. The uninflated prior was overconfident: the truth sat inside its 95% region in about half of periods. On this seed it harmed Annex B periods that had an ownship turn of their own (0.51).
  • The choice. Five variants were run: inflation by 2 or 4 in sd, and mixtures with the standing prior. A rule written before the results kept only variants with no own-turn harm and coverage of at least 0.80. It chose k4, the covariance 4 times wider in sd.
  • Seed 360. A declared check passed here.

How it was decided​

All comparisons use periods after an engagement's first, on spec 025's rows. Each is a ratio of period median range error, with a 95% interval from resampling engagements.

  • Helps: ctl alone ÷ k4 in range is wholly above 1 on Annex B, the split that decides.
  • Harms: wholly below 1 in range, course or speed on any split, or in range on Annex B periods with their own ownship turn.

Validation used seed 362, where soundness passed. The test used seed 363, scored once.

The result​

splitalone ÷ k4, range (median per period)k4 ÷ joint, range
Annex B (decides)1.59 [1.21, 2.13] (1.09): helps1.40 [0.98, 2.01]
busier targets1.60 [1.28, 1.99] (1.16)1.25 [0.94, 1.66]
2% wild bearings1.35 [1.01, 1.87] (1.01)1.74 [1.23, 2.43]
held course2.32 [1.49, 3.62] (1.27)5.20 [2.93, 9.00]

No harm on any split in any quantity. On Annex B periods with their own turn the ratio is 1.22 [0.84, 1.85]. On Annex B, k4 is better in 57% of periods and worse in 32%. It is twice as good in 32% and twice as bad in 11%.

What it means, as the panel narrowed it​

  • The gain is where the bearings leave a period undetermined.
    • Annex B periods without their own ownship turn: 1.97. With one: 1.22.
    • On rows a period determines by itself: 1.04 [0.77, 1.48], level.
    • So a carried prior makes undetermined periods answerable. It does not improve a period's own estimate. This is the same pattern as spec 025's joint solve.
  • The inflation is not shown to matter.
    • The uninflated prior does as well on the test seed: uninflated ÷ k4 is 0.99 [0.78, 1.25].
    • The uninflated prior would also have passed the rule.
    • The own-turn harm that motivated k4 appeared on one development seed only.
    • What is supported is "a carried prior helps", not "inflate by 4".
  • k4's uncertainty is too wide, not calibrated.
    • It covers the truth (0.92 to 0.98) because its spread is about 2.6 times too wide: median squared distance 0.51 against 3.36 for a calibrated prior.
    • The process noise is mis-shaped. It puts half of a turn's change into speed, and constant velocity runs the mean ahead of a turning target.
    • A single history's covariance is too narrow in the tail even with no manoeuvre in the gap.
    • After inflation the prior carries little beyond a band on position.
  • Against the alternatives.
    • Against spec 027's carried start (not registered): 1.60 [1.05, 2.74] on Annex B.
    • Against joining: on the line on Annex B (lower limit 0.97 to 1.02 by bootstrap seed). Separated with wild bearings and on held course.
    • Joining is not shown unnecessary anywhere.
  • Across seeds. Annex B alone ÷ k4 was 1.59, 1.22, 1.51 and 1.59 on seeds 360 to 363. The one that would not pass (361) is the seed k4 was chosen on.
  • When it applies.
    • Within this simulator, when only the previous declared state and its covariance are kept, a period solved under them is better than one solved from nothing.
    • Time-late, the earlier bearings are normally kept, and then the joint solve is the answer.
    • A real hand-over was not tested: a track from another estimator, with uncertain association.
  • Secondary splits are reported, not decided.
    • Wild bearings is on the line and carried by a tail (median 1.01).
    • Held course's 2.32 is measured against a baseline that is very poor there.

Forecasts​

Right:

  • helps on Annex B (1.59, against a forecast of 1.2 to 1.6), with one development seed in two failing;
  • busier about 1.55 (1.60), held course larger, no harm.

Wrong:

  • k4 ÷ joint on Annex B (forecast about 2.1; 1.40, on the line).
  • Coverage was "right" (0.92 to 0.98), but by being too wide.

What was not done​

  • A calibrated carried uncertainty: a scale near 1.5, noise shaped to turns and speed changes, or a prior over the previous period's candidate histories.
  • A registered comparison of k4 with the uninflated prior and with the carried start.
  • Code that applies the rule: the verdict was applied by hand.
  • IMM and EKF tracks.

Recorded, not repaired (the code is registered):

  • the wrapped course Gaussian is normalised on the line, not the circle;
  • a speed shoulder is left in the fit;
  • three small fragilities.

What next (the owner's choice)​

The panel's order:

  1. A consistency flag. Compare the carried prior's distance with the period's own fit, and test whether it finds the twice-as-bad periods.
  2. A calibrated carried prior on spent seeds. Scale, shaped noise, the manoeuvre mixture and candidate histories.
  3. A stress split with longer gaps and more periods, where a carried state is the realistic option.
  4. A real hand-over. Only if that case matters: a carried state from another estimator, with uncertain association.

This study was developed and registered as spec 028 and renumbered 030 after another session's specs 028 and 029 merged first; its registered seeds 362 and 363 had also been claimed by spec 029 in the long-engagement simulator (different engagements; recorded in the decision record).

Records:

  • spec specs/030-carried-prior/;
  • development experiments/20261119-tl10-dev/ and refinement 20261119-tl10-refine/;
  • decision 20261119-tl10-decision/;
  • validation 20261119-tl10-val/;
  • test 20261120-tl10/, with the panel's review.md and supplement.json.

item.title: Kickoff: several periods of one target across long gaps
item.description: Spec 030 found that a carried prior helps a period that cannot answer alone, while one solve
item.content:encoded:
Spec 030 found that a carried prior helps a period that cannot answer alone, while one solve through the gaps stays the better choice. Both findings come from gaps of 5 to 30 minutes. This task stretches the gaps to 30–90 minutes, with up to four periods, where joining has to bridge hours of unseen manoeuvres. Nothing is trained.

Where we are​

  • Spec 030: the carried prior helps against solving each period alone (1.59 on Annex B), but is not shown equal to the joint solve.
  • A per-period consistency flag was judged not worth registering: the periods it would need to catch are mostly ones where ctl alone happened to land close.

Where this task moves to​

  • Spec specs/033-long-gaps/: 6-hour engagements from the long simulator (ownship legs of 20–40 minutes, Annex B targets), laid out as 2–4 periods with gaps of 30–90 minutes.
  • Spec 030's systems run unchanged: ctl alone, the joint solve, the carried start, and the carried prior both uninflated and as k4.
  • Development first, on a spent seed. Then a proposal: register on fresh seeds, or stop.
  • Risks:
    • the joint solve over 3–4 hours may hit ctl's cap of ten manoeuvres, and it costs more;
    • the long simulator's ownship steers on the true target.

How progress will be shown​

  • The ratios by gap length and by whether a period has its own ownship turn.
  • The joint solve's cost and how often it meets the cap.
  • How often the truth falls inside the carried prior's stated uncertainty.

item.title: Kickoff: the carried prior against longer windows and a joint solve
item.description: Spec 029 found that when the ownship holds course, carrying the
item.content:encoded:
Spec 029 found that when the ownship holds course, carrying the previous window's state as a prior roughly halves the error on turn-free 1-hour windows. That was measured against the same blind window solved alone.

The owner asked for the comparison that matters in practice: the prior against ctl on its standing 2-hour windows, and against a joint solve over two windows. Spec: specs/031-held-comparators/.

Where we are​

  • Prior against the same window alone: on turn-free 1-hour windows, ctl ÷ ctl-prior is 2.41 [2.06, 2.83] (spec 029).
  • What is still open: whether the hand-over is a cheap substitute for using the earlier bearings directly.

Where this task moves to​

  • The three systems, on spec 029's held-course engagements (tended contact):
    • (a) ctl-prior on 1-hour windows;
    • (b) ctl on 2-hour windows overlapping 30 min, stitched;
    • (c) ctl on the union of each turn-free hour and the hour before it.
  • Rules:
    • D1 = (b) ÷ (a) and D2 = (c) ÷ (a), on turn-free windows, with a bootstrap over engagements.
    • Each ends "ctl-prior better", "ctl-prior worse" or "not separated".
  • Plan:
    1. tuning on spent seed 364 (12 engagements);
    2. the decision record;
    3. validation on seed 365;
    4. test on seed 366, scored once;
    5. the panel, then the write-up.
  • Risks:
    • (b) and (c) see more bearings and may simply win.
    • Compute is about 100 runner-hours on the test.

How progress will be shown​

  • D1 and D2 with intervals.
  • Per-window ratios.
  • Compute per window for each system.
  • A track plot of one turn-free hour under all three.

item.content:encoded:
These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up. The ownship holds each leg for 1–2 hours. On 1-hour windows with no ownship turn, the previous window's state, carried as a prior, gives ctl ÷ ctl-prior 2.41 [2.06, 2.83], against the same window alone. The registered rule says gain, with no harm. Spec: specs/029-held-course/.

What was built​

  • Configs: configs/long/hold-{tuning,val,test}.json, which hold the ownship's legs to 1–2 h.
  • CI: long.yml passes the window length and overlap through.
  • The scorer: src/tma2/long/study29.py, run by tma2-long study29. It classifies windows by ownship turns, applies the rule, and reads coverage and soundness.
  • Scripts: scripts/research/hold_{digests,supplement,charts}.py.
  • Records:
    • tuning: experiments/20261119-hold-tuning/;
    • decision: 20261119-hold-decision/;
    • validation: 20261119-hold-val/;
    • test: 20261119-hold/, with review.md and supplement.json.

What was not achieved​

  • Untested comparisons: ctl on 2-hour windows, and a joint solve over consecutive windows.
  • Not measured: whether the prior narrows the set of manoeuvre histories.
  • Untested settings: the untended contact, and real data.
  • Kept defect: spec 028's hand-over defect.

What comes next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended: adopt ctl-prior with its guard for the tended contact. Then run one registered comparison against 2-hour ctl and a joint solve, on held-course engagements.
  • Alternatives:
    • repair the hand-over;
    • the untended contact under held course;
    • close the track.

Figures: scripts/research/hold_charts.py, with a sidecar beside each SVG.

item.title: Long engagements: the carried prior where the ownship holds course
item.description: The owner's hypothesis was that knowledge of the previous track can usefully constrain the
item.content:encoded:
The owner's hypothesis was that knowledge of the previous track can usefully constrain the solution for the next leg. Spec 028 could not test it, because its ownship never held course long enough to leave a window blind. This study makes the ownship hold each leg for one to two hours.

Result:

  • The registered rule says gain, with no harm.
  • On 1-hour windows that contain no ownship turn, carrying the previous window's state as a prior gives ctl ÷ ctl-prior 2.41 [2.06, 2.83]. The median window improves 2.15-fold.
  • The comparison is against the same window solved alone.

Spec: specs/029-held-course/. Record: experiments/20261119-hold/.

The design​

  • Engagements: spec 024's simulated realism, with ownship legs of 1–2 h, the tended contact only.
  • Windows:
    • With such legs, no 2-hour window is free of turns. Holds long enough to change that lose the target beyond detection.
    • So windows are 1 hour, overlapping 15 minutes. That gives about 30% of windows with no ownship turn.
  • Systems: spec 028's ctl-prior, at its registered settings, is compared with ctl on the same windows. ctl-prior carries the previous window's state and uncertainty, fitted on bearings before the hand-over, into the next window's fit and evidence, with a guard.
  • Rule (registered before seeds 363 and 364 existed):
    • Gain if the lower limit on turn-free windows is above 1.
    • Harm if any class's upper limit is below 1.
    • Windows where nothing was handed on are excluded, and the bootstrap is over engagements.

What happened​

Test: seed 364, 60 engagements of 6 and 12 hours, scored once.

windowsctl ÷ ctl-prior, rangemedian windowbetter
no ownship turn (registered)2.41 [2.06, 2.83]2.1576%
one ownship turn1.22 [1.06, 1.40]1.1259%
  • Course and speed on turn-free windows: 1.96 and 2.24.
  • Median range error on turn-free windows: from 22.7% to 7.4%.
  • Agreement across seeds: tuning 2.10, validation 1.91, test 2.41.
  • The prior's own effect: the carried start alone does little (1.14) and costs 11% on one-turn windows. The prior does the work: ctl-carry ÷ ctl-prior is 2.12.
  • Guard: it fell back on 0.9% of windows.
  • Soundness: all checks passed; held-window coverage was 0.945.

What the panel narrowed​

Three reviewers, each approve with findings (experiments/20261119-hold/review.md):

  • The comparator is a window chosen to be blind. The result says the predecessor's state beats the same 1-hour window alone. Two comparisons were not tested: ctl on its usual 2-hour windows, and a joint solve over consecutive windows.
  • The mechanism is range observability. The previous track constrains this leg's solution where the leg alone cannot resolve range. Whether it narrows the set of manoeuvre histories was not measured.
  • The gain grows with range: 1.66 under 15 km, 2.15 at 15–25 km, 3.19 beyond 25 km. Holding course pushes range up, so the pooled figure depends on this simulator's range mix. On one-turn windows the gain is not separated from 1 under 15 km.
  • The excluded turn-free windows are windows where contact was lost. Counted as ties, the result is 2.34.
  • The coverage figure (0.945) passes the band but is not a calibration. The region is too wide for most hand-overs.
  • Limits:
    • one simulator, contact 1 only, 1-hour windows;
    • hand-overs never fall inside a target manoeuvre, because windows are placed by truth;
    • spec 028's hand-over defect is kept.
  • ctl-carry should not be used without the prior.

What it means for the owner's question​

The previous track helps a great deal exactly where the owner expected: where the leg's own bearings cannot fix range. In this simulator, on the tended contact, the median error on such windows falls by about two-thirds. Spec 028's small average shift was the same mechanism in windows that rarely needed it.

Next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended default:
    • Adopt ctl-prior with its guard as the standing chained time-late system for the tended contact.
    • Next, one registered comparison on held-course engagements, each system on its own windows: ctl-prior on 1-hour windows, ctl on 2-hour windows, and a joint solve over two consecutive windows, with a reference told the truth over the span. This asks whether the prior is a cheap substitute for using the bearings themselves.
  • Alternatives:
    • repair the hand-over (a neutral refit start) and rerun on spent seeds;
    • the untended contact under held course;
    • close the long-engagement track here.

Slides: the slides post.

item.title: Kickoff: the carried prior where the ownship holds course
item.description: Spec 028 carried the previous window's state and uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Spec 028 carried the previous window's state and uncertainty into the next window as a prior. It found a small average shift and no harm, but it could not test the owner's own case. In that simulator the ownship turned every 20–40 minutes, so every window could resolve the target from its own bearings. The owner asked to test the ownship holding course. This study does that. Spec: specs/029-held-course/.

Where we are​

  • Standing time-late system: ctl. ctl-prior is recommended for adoption, scoped as "a small refinement, no harm shown".
  • Spec 028's registered split showed no gain: 1.105 [0.963, 1.273]. That split was mostly the untended contact. The owner's case never occurred.

Where this task moves to​

  • Engagements: realistic engagements where the ownship holds each leg for 1–2 hours, tended contact only.
  • Windows: 1-hour windows overlapping 15 minutes. With 2-hour windows no window is free of ownship turns.
  • Turn-free windows: about 30% of windows contain no ownship turn (measured on spent seed 354).
  • Rule:
    • Gain if ctl ÷ ctl-prior on turn-free windows has its lower limit above 1, with a bootstrap over engagements.
    • Harm if any class's upper limit is below 1, in range, course or speed.
    • Windows where nothing was handed on are excluded.
  • Plan:
    1. tuning on seed 362 checks the split and the carried prior's coverage;
    2. the decision record;
    3. validation on seed 363;
    4. test on seed 364, scored once;
    5. the panel, then the write-up.
  • Risks:
    • Holding course costs range keeping: the target drifts to 50 km at the 95th percentile, beyond detection, so geometry and detection mix.
    • The carried prior's settings were set on 2-hour windows.
    • The hand-over defect spec 028's panel found stays in.
  • Stop: soundness or coverage outside its band on validation.

How progress will be shown​

  • ctl ÷ ctl-prior by class (no turn, one turn, more), with intervals.
  • Per-window ratios.
  • Coverage of the carried prior on turn-free windows.
  • A track plot of a turn-free window.

item.title: Slides: the previous window as a prior
item.description: These slides are the illustrated companion to
item.content:encoded:
These slides are the illustrated companion to the write-up. The registered rule's output is not shown, at this size, with no harm. Beside the rule, carrying the previous window's state as a prior gives a small average shift: about 10% in geometric mean and 3% in the median window. Spec: specs/028-carry-prior/.

What was built​

  • src/tma2/long/carried.py: the carried prior.
    • The fit and evidence carry it as a Gaussian term. With no prior they equal the originals, which a unit test checks.
    • The hand-over excludes the next window's bearings.
    • It also holds the widening and the χ²(4) guard.
  • src/tma2/long/carry2.py: ctl-prior beside ctl and ctl-carry in one job. A test checks that ctl and ctl-carry equal spec 026's.
  • src/tma2/long/study27.py: the scorer. CLI: tma2-long carry2, study27 and jointpair.
  • CI: long.yml now ignores pushes to main and pushes its results to an orphan branch.
  • Records:
    • tuning experiments/20261118-cp-tuning/;
    • decision 20261119-cp-decision/;
    • validation 20261119-cp-val/;
    • test 20261119-cp/, with review.md, supplement.json and ties.json.

What was not achieved​

  • The owner's case: a window without useful ownship geometry does not occur in this simulator.
  • Gain on the registered split: not shown.
  • Whether the prior narrows the set of histories: not tested.
  • The hand-over defect: the refit's start is recorded, not repaired.

What comes next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended: adopt ctl-prior with its guard for tended contacts up to 12 hours, then close the track.
  • Alternatives:
    • an ownship that holds course for one to two hours, which answers the owner's question directly;
    • a registered joint solve over consecutive windows.

Figures: scripts/research/cp_charts.py, with a sidecar beside each SVG.

item.title: Long engagements: the previous window as a prior
item.description: Spec 026 found that handing the previous 2-hour window's track to the next window as a starting
item.content:encoded:
Spec 026 found that handing the previous 2-hour window's track to the next window as a starting guess changed nothing in accuracy. The owner expected more: "knowledge of the previous track can usefully constrain the range of permutations for this leg".

This study tests that expectation as a prior. The previous window hands on its estimate of the target's position, course and speed at the next window's first row, with its uncertainty. That estimate enters the next window's fit and the evidence that ranks manoeuvre histories.

The registered rule's output is not shown, at this size, with no harm anywhere. Beside the rule, the prior gives a small average shift: about 10% in geometric mean and 3% in the median window. Spec: specs/028-carry-prior/. Record: experiments/20261119-cp/.

What was registered​

Design (decision record experiments/20261119-cp-decision/, before seeds 355 and 356 existed):

  • Systems: ctl, ctl-carry (spec 026's carried start) and ctl-prior are solved on every window of a chain, in one job per contact.
  • The hand-over:
    • The carried estimate uses no bearing the next window also uses.
    • Its Laplace covariance is scaled by 4 and widened for manoeuvres the earlier bearings could not yet show.
    • A χ²(4) guard drops the prior where the window's own bearings reject it.

The rule: ctl ÷ ctl-prior per window, with the engagement bootstrap and each chain's first window excluded.

  • Gain: the lower limit is above 1 on windows of weak geometry: the untended contact, a window near a contact gap, or one with at most one ownship turn.
  • Harm: an upper limit is below 1 on any split, in range, course or speed.

What happened​

Test (seed 356, 60 realistic engagements of 6 and 12 hours, both contacts, scored once):

splitctl ÷ ctl-prior, range
weak geometry (registered)1.105 [0.963, 1.273]
other windows of the tended contact1.14 [1.035, 1.27]
tended contact1.11 [1.006, 1.22]
untended contact1.16 [0.988, 1.37]

The panel's sensitivities do not change the outcome:

  • clustered by engagement, the weak split is 1.105 [0.951, 1.279];
  • without the 13 windows where nothing was handed on, it is 1.112 [0.964, 1.297].

Soundness:

  • 720 of 720 windows ran.
  • On the tended contact, the carried 95% region covered the truth 95.3% of the time.

What the panel narrowed​

The panel was three reviewers, each approve with findings (experiments/20261119-cp/review.md).

  • The owner's case was not sampled. The ownship turns every 20–40 minutes, so a window with no useful ownship manoeuvre never occurs in this simulator. The weak split is in effect the untended contact plus windows near gaps. On the gap windows of the tended contact the ratio is 0.98 [0.79, 1.25].
  • What the prior does, beside the rule:
    • About 1.1 in geometric mean on the tended contact's ordinary windows, in range and course, on validation and test.
    • The median window is 1.03 and 44% of windows are worse. That is an average shift with many losses.
    • It is not concentrated where the declared manoeuvre count changed. Whether the same history was kept was not tested.
    • So "narrows the permutations" is not shown, either way.
  • The prior against the carried start alone: ctl-carry ÷ ctl-prior is 1.14 to 1.22 on every split. On this seed ctl-carry itself was level with ctl (0.95).
  • The guard did what it was for. It fell back on 8 of 443 windows. There, the unguarded answer was 1.85 times ctl's error.
  • Forecasts: two of five were wrong, the other split's sign and the coverage level. Twelve tuning engagements had no forecast value.
  • Registration:
    • The registered settings were extrapolated from a grid, not run as a chain on tuning.
    • The coverage check covered only the tended contact, while the decided split is mostly the untended one (coverage 0.76 on validation).
  • A recorded defect: the hand-over's refit starts from the full window's fit. On flat valleys it can keep information from the overlap, counting those bearings twice. At this study's scale coverage did not show it.

What it costs​

The prior's searches add about 24% to the run's search time. The fit told the true manoeuvre history is still 0.72 to 0.86 times ctl-prior's error. On 12 tuning pairs, spec 025's joint solve over two windows was 1.7 times better, at three times the time.

Next (the owner's choice)​

  • Recommended default: adopt ctl-prior, with its guard, as the standing chained system for tended contacts up to 12 hours, scoped as "a small refinement, no harm shown". Then close the long-engagement track as a simulation study.
  • The test that answers the owner's question: a simulator option where the ownship holds course for one to two hours, with ctl-prior scored there. It is cheap.
  • The larger lead: a registered joint solve over consecutive windows. It is 1.7 times better on 12 pairs, at three times the cost.

Slides: the slides post.

item.title: Kickoff: a carried prior across gaps
item.description: Spec 027 showed that handing the next period only a starting point does almost nothing:
item.content:encoded:
Spec 027 showed that handing the next period only a starting point does almost nothing: the period's own bearings decide. This task hands it a prior: the previous period's state and uncertainty, run through the gap with room for a manoeuvre the gap may hide, inside the next period's evidence. It is the sequential approximation to the joint solve, scored first on spent seeds (owner, option A). Nothing is trained.

Where we are​

  • Spec 027: joining beats a carried start (Annex B 2.33 [1.66, 3.43]); the carried start ties with ctl alone in about half of periods.
  • The joint solve is the standing time-late system for several periods of one target.

Where this task moves to​

  • Spec specs/030-carried-prior/: a Gaussian prior on each later period's starting state, applied through wrappers so no registered code changes; equal to ctl with no prior.
  • Development readings on spec 027's spent test engagements: carried prior against joining, against ctl alone and against the carried start; and whether the carried uncertainty is honest.
  • Then a proposal: register a study on fresh seeds, or stop.
  • Risk, already seen on three engagements: the previous period's Laplace uncertainty is overconfident where its fit is wrong, so the prior can pull the next period away from the truth.

How progress will be shown​

  • The ratios by split and by kind of period; how often the truth falls inside the carried two-sigma ellipse.

The illustrated companion to the spec 027 write-up: the registered comparison, how often the carry changes anything, and where.

What the figures show​

  • Ties: the share of later periods where the carry is within 1% of ctl alone, better or worse.

item.title: Carrying state across gaps: a carried start does not substitute for joining
item.description: Spec 025 showed that one solve over several periods of a target beats solving each period
item.content:encoded:
Spec 025 showed that one solve over several periods of a target beats solving each period alone. The cheaper habit is to solve period by period and hand each answer on to the next. This registered study measured that habit against the joint solve. By the rule registered beforehand, joining is better on Annex B targets, and the carry shows no effect over solving alone there. The review panel approved and narrowed the result. What was tested is a carried start, not carried information, so the study says nothing yet about carrying a prior. Nothing was trained. The illustrated companion is the slides post.

What was built​

The carry solves each period in order, on that period's own bearings. In the standing control ctl, the search starts from two places: C″'s answer and a start from nothing. The carry replaces the start from nothing with the previous period's declared state at its last row, run forward at constant velocity through the gap. Everything else is ctl, as spec 024 designed its carry for overlapping windows. With no carried state the code reproduces ctl exactly, and every run checks this on each engagement's first period. Spec 024's own carry was not run: it carries over rows that windows share, and across a gap there are none.

How it was decided​

All comparisons are over periods after an engagement's first, on spec 025's rows. Each is a per-period ratio of period median range error, with a 95% interval from resampling engagements.

  • Carry ÷ joint: "joining better" if the interval is wholly above 1, "carry better" if wholly below.
  • Alone ÷ carry: "carrying helps" if the interval is wholly above 1; "carrying harms" if the interval is wholly below 1 in range, course or speed.

Annex B decides.

  • Seeds: tuning on spent seed 353, validation 360 (soundness passed), test 361, scored once.

The result​

splitcarry ÷ jointalone ÷ carry
Annex B (decides)2.33 [1.66, 3.43]: joining better1.07 [0.88, 1.34]: not shown
busier targets1.351 [0.993, 1.820]: not separated1.29 [1.09, 1.54]: helps
2% wild bearings3.57 [2.21, 5.68]: joining better1.10: not shown
held course10.5 [5.5, 19.8]: joining better1.27: not shown

No harm on any split in any quantity. The joint solve stays the standing system for several periods of one target, within spec 025's conditions.

What it means, as the panel narrowed it​

  • Joining had to win. Nothing from the earlier period enters the period's likelihood or prior; only where the search starts changes. Even the per-period fit told the true manoeuvre history is 8.4 times worse than joining on these rows (Annex B). So the study shows where the information is. It does not show what carrying, done properly, is worth.
  • The carry rarely changes the answer. About half of later periods end exactly where ctl alone does. On busier targets the carry helps in about a quarter of periods, about twice as good there, almost all where the period has no ownship turn of its own (1.72). That is a different minimum of a poorly determined fit, not an answer the bearings endorse.
  • No harm shown, which is not the same as no cost. Annex B periods with their own turn read 0.91 [0.78, 1.02]. A wrong carried state replaces the start from nothing, which is the carry's only way to do harm.
  • Busier targets. The range interval misses "joining better" by 0.007; joining is better in course and speed. For a busier period that stands alone, neither joining (spec 025: 1.06) nor carrying is shown to help.
  • No recommendation. The first record recommended the carry where a joint solve is unavailable. The rule recommends it only if it helps on Annex B, which it does not, so the recommendation is withdrawn.
  • What "not shown" excludes. On Annex B the interval rules out harm worse than about 12% and gains above about a third, and nothing smaller.

Forecasts​

Right:

  • joining better on Annex B (about 2.2; 2.33);
  • carrying not shown on Annex B;
  • carrying helping a little on busier targets (1.29, larger than forecast).

Wrong:

  • joining better on busier targets (not separated, by a hair);
  • held course about 4 (it was 10.5);
  • a harm in held-course speed (none).

What was not done​

  • A carried prior.
  • A test of the carry chain in the unit tests.
  • IMM and EKF tracks.

What next (the owner's choice)​

The panel's order:

  1. A carried prior. The previous period's state and covariance, widened through the gap by Annex B's manoeuvre rates, used as a prior in the period's evidence. Scored on spent seeds first, this decides whether joining is needed at all.
  2. A consistency flag. A per-period flag for a failed join, and markers on inferred gap manoeuvres.
  3. An uncertainty. A stated uncertainty for the joined track.
  4. Longer gaps. Gaps longer than 30 minutes.

Records: decision experiments/20261118-tl9-decision/, tuning 20261118-tl9-tuning/, validation 20261118-tl9-val/, test 20261119-tl9/ with the panel's review.md. Spec specs/027-carry-across-gaps/.

item.title: Kickoff: carrying the previous window as a prior
item.description: Spec 026's ctl-carry gave each 2-hour window the previous window's track as a starting guess.
item.content:encoded:
Spec 026's ctl-carry gave each 2-hour window the previous window's track as a starting guess. It found the same answers faster but no better ones, because nothing in the fit itself changed. The owner expected knowledge of the previous track to narrow the hypotheses for the next window. This study tests that expectation directly. The previous window's estimate and its uncertainty enter the next window's fit, and the evidence that ranks manoeuvre histories, as a prior. Spec: specs/028-carry-prior/.

Where we are​

  • Spec 026's registered study found carrying a starting guess level with solving each window cold. The ratio was 1.021 [0.950, 1.100] without the first windows, which are equal by construction. The search was 31% cheaper. A gain of up to about 10% was not excluded.
  • The standing time-late system is ctl. It scores 1.5–2.2% median range error on a tended contact and 1.3–1.5 times worse on an untended one.
  • Spec 025 showed what a real constraint across time can win. Solving periods jointly gained about 3× on Annex B targets, mostly where a period had no ownship turn of its own.

Where this task moves to​

  • SRD §1. A registered study, not a gate. Nothing is trained and nothing runs on GPU.
  • Rule: gain if the geometric mean of ctl ÷ ctl-prior per window has its lower limit above 1 on the weak-geometry split. Weak geometry means the untended contact, a window after a contact gap, or a window with at most one ownship turn. Harm if any split's upper limit is below 1, in range, course or speed. Each chain's first window is excluded.
  • Safeguards:
    • the carried estimate uses no bearing the next window also uses;
    • its uncertainty is widened for manoeuvres it cannot yet see;
    • a chi-square guard drops the prior where the window's bearings reject it.
  • Plan:
    1. build ctl-prior beside ctl and ctl-carry, solved in the same job;
    2. tune the widening and the guard's level on seed 354, and check the weak-geometry split has at least 100 windows;
    3. write the decision record and its forecasts;
    4. validate on seed 355, including a coverage check of the carried prior;
    5. score the test on seed 356 (30 + 30 engagements of 6 and 12 hours) once;
    6. run the agent review panel, then publish the write-up.
  • Risks:
    • Laplace covariances have been overconfident before. An overconfident prior pulls each window towards the last window's mistakes.
    • A Gaussian prior on one state cannot hand on a second-best manoeuvre history.
    • A gain confined to the untended contact would describe this simulator.
  • Stop: the study stops before the test if the carried prior's coverage falls outside its declared band, or if spec 026's soundness checks fail on validation.

How progress will be shown​

  • ctl ÷ ctl-prior per window, by split and contact, with the registered interval against 1.
  • The prior's own effect, ctl-carry ÷ ctl-prior, window by window along a chain.
  • The carried prior's 95% coverage and the guard's fall-back rate.
  • A track plot of one weak-geometry chain: truth, ctl, ctl-prior.
  • All from the test record on seed 356, with tuning seed 354 for the design figures.
